# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date you are sending this letter]

**To:** Avera Health Plans — Member Appeals
[Use the appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:**
Quinn Delgado
[Street address]
[City, SD ZIP]
[Phone] | [Email]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026-08-17**
- **Member name:** Quinn Delgado
- **Member ID:** W570305899
- **Reference number:** POC-A389519C6D-33639
- **Denied service:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
- **Plan / product:** Avera Health Plans, Commercial/ACA, South Dakota
- **Governing policy:** Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index (Knee Arthroplasty v8, Knee Arthroscopy v10, Hip Arthroplasty v5, Hip Arthroscopy v6, Shoulder Arthroplasty v4, Shoulder Arthroscopy v5, Open Shoulder v4, Cervical Spinal Fusion v5, Lumbar Spinal Fusion v3, Spinal Decompression v4.1, Ankle Arthroplasty v4, Great Toe Surgical Treatments v3) — https://help.coherehealth.com/payer-info/en/articles/13602157-avera-health-plan-commercial-guidelines

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296, which Avera Health Plans denied on 2026-08-17 as not medically necessary. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and to approve the procedure. My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, MD, orthopedic surgery, submitted the request and documented in my chart that this surgery is needed.

## The criteria the plan applied have not been given to me in full

The governing policy for this decision is the Cohere Health: Avera Commercial Guidelines index listed above. The published index I can access states, verbatim:

> "All Collections Review Criteria Avera Health Plan Avera Health Plan:"

and

> "Commercial/Medicaid & Medicare Advantage Guidelines Review Criteria:"

That index names the guidelines Avera uses, including a guideline for great toe surgical treatments. What it does not give me is the text of the clinical requirements that were applied to my request. I want to be straightforward with the reviewer about that: **beyond the lines above, I am not quoting plan criteria in this letter, because the specific criteria language used to deny my surgery has not been provided to me.** Everything that follows is my own description of what my medical records show.

## What my records show

Because I cannot match my chart line by line to criteria I have not been given, I am setting out the documented facts that Dr. Marchetti submitted with the prior authorization request. These are the findings that are typically at issue in a medical-necessity review of bunion surgery:

**Duration and persistence of symptoms.** I have had 18 months of progressive pain in the foot. The pain is not relieved by rest.

**Conservative (non-surgical) treatment, tried and completed.** I completed activity modification, wide toe-box footwear, and a custom orthotic over 12 weeks, from 2026-04-02 to 2026-06-25, with 20 visits completed. This is documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

**Medication trials.** I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief. I also received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-04, which gave me only 3 weeks of partial relief.

**Objective imaging.** Weight-bearing foot radiographs taken 2026-06-07 show a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees.

**Examination findings.** My exam showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.

**Functional impact.** I cannot tolerate closed shoes, and there is ulceration risk over the bony prominence.

**No contraindications to surgery.** I have no active infection and no untreated substance use. My BMI is 29 and I am a non-smoker.

In short, this is not a request made before conservative care was tried. Non-surgical treatment was carried out over a defined 12-week course, medication and injection were tried, and the deformity is documented on weight-bearing x-ray. If the plan's guideline requires a documented trial of conservative care, objective imaging of the deformity, and functional limitation, my record contains each of those things in writing.

## Please send me the criteria you used

I am asking Avera Health Plans, in writing, to provide **the exact clinical criteria applied to this denial**, including the name and edition or version number of any review guideline relied on, and the specific requirement or requirements my request was found not to meet. The plan holds these criteria; I do not. I am entitled to them, and I cannot fully respond to the determination without them. If the denial rests on a criterion my records already satisfy, I ask that it be corrected on reconsideration. If it rests on something my records do not yet address, please tell me what it is so my surgeon and I can supply it.

## What I am asking for

I ask that Avera Health Plans overturn the denial dated 2026-08-17 (reference POC-A389519C6D-33639) and authorize bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296, as requested by Dr. Marchetti. I also ask that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic or foot and ankle surgery, and that I receive the written criteria requested above.

Per the denial notice, this appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of the notice — **by 2027-02-13**. I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if that is not the correct destination, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed, and I ask that the plan redirect this letter internally so it is not delayed.

Please send your decision to me in writing at the address above, and copy Dr. Marchetti. I am glad to provide any additional records you need — you may contact me at [Phone] or [Email].

Thank you for reviewing this again.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Delgado**
Member ID: W570305899
Reference: POC-A389519C6D-33639

**Enclosures:** [List what you are sending — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-17; physical therapy discharge note; weight-bearing radiograph report dated 2026-06-07; office notes from Dr. Marchetti; injection record dated 2026-05-04]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
